stemMd: A spherical cell doubles its radius while retaining the same shape. How does its surface-area-to-volume ratio change?
explanationMd: For a sphere, area is proportional to radius squared and volume to radius cubed. Doubling radius multiplies area by 4 and volume by 8, so their ratio is multiplied by 4/8, or one half.

distractorRationale.d: Geometrical similarity does not preserve area-to-volume ratio.
distractorRationale.a: This is the volume factor, not the ratio factor.
distractorRationale.b: Area grows more slowly than volume.
distractorRationale.c: This is the area factor, not the ratio factor.
